key_insight: World Action Models can do more than predict robot actions: they can also generate future visual observations. REGEN uses this generative ability to create pseudo-replay trajectories, letting a robot keep learning new tasks without forgetting old ones or storing the original human demos.
problem_solved: Continual imitation learning often suffers from catastrophic forgetting and depends on retaining past human demonstrations. This paper addresses how to preserve previously learned robot behaviors while adapting to new tasks without keeping the full demonstration dataset.
method: Leverages a World Action Model (WAM) to synthesize future observation-action sequences.
Uses Recurrent Generative Replay (REGEN) to recursively generate pseudo-replay trajectories during continual training.
Trains the policy on synthetic replay data so it can rehearse prior tasks while learning new ones, reducing the need for stored demonstrations.
impact: This approach offers a practical path toward scalable lifelong robot learning with lower memory requirements. For AI/ML practitioners, it shows how generative world models can support continual learning by replacing stored replay buffers with synthetic experience.
